feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: it communicates scope, progression, and relevant platform expertise clearly. The content is polished and substantive, but it is slightly dense and somewhat repetitive across sections, which reduces impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression at NACo strongly support leadership credibility in digital platforms, communications, and governance.  
- Good use of scale and specificity: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools/platforms add impact and trust.  
- Broad but coherent skill set: strategy, CMS/platform delivery, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are well aligned for modern digital leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and readability.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more measurable results beyond activity/scale would strengthen impact.  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual unless intentional; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma); “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary filler. No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language: “leading” or “delivering.”
- Add one high-value proof point from recent work, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Tighten the second sentence to emphasize strategic scope over a long list of functions.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web platforms, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Delivers enterprise website modernization, editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations, including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” repeats ideas already covered in Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
- The subtitle already signals leadership; avoid repeating broad “digital leader” language elsewhere.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened, made slightly more distinctive, and aligned in style.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and trim filler: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership”
- Clarify higher-value differentiators: “AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations”
- Consider replacing “website” with “web” for a more senior, enterprise tone.
- Standardize “and” vs “&” across the CV; “and” reads cleaner and more formal.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section repeats several phrases from the header almost verbatim, especially “enterprise web modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” “editorial systems,” and “AI-enabled user/content experiences.”
- It also overlaps with Topline Skills; consider making this block broader and using Topline Skills for the detailed breakdown.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots that reinforce your current positioning, but the block is too dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. It will land better with tighter formatting, parallel phrasing, and clearer emphasis on recency.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add dates or a “Selected Recent Projects” label to signal recency and distinguish this from core experience.
- Use concise, parallel one-line entries: project name + scope + outcome/value.
- Tighten wording: “AI-enabled” appears multiple times across the CV; vary phrasing and remove filler like “designed for continued campaign growth.”
- Standardize style and punctuation, including “10 x 20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot” unless that symbol is used consistently elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with the current freelance role and NACo bullets; keep this block more portfolio-style, not responsibility-style.
- “Editorial storytelling,” “web features,” and “production/distribution across channels” echo existing competencies and work history; focus on what was uniquely built or achieved.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Core Competencies

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the project footer and prior NACo entries. Tighten around strategic ownership, platform impact, and 1–2 concrete outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Lead digital strategy, platform modernization, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization in a full-time freelance engagement.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4 focused points: enterprise systems/analytics, Drupal campaign builds, cross-channel governance, and AI-enabled search leadership.
- Replace generic phrasing like “support,” “advise,” and “deliver” with stronger verbs: “lead,” “design,” “build,” “standardize,” “optimize.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, workflow time saved, publishing speed improved, search/discovery gains, toolkit downloads, or stakeholder teams enabled.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” and Drupal microsite work duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and let the footer hold examples.
- “Governance, usability, and operational best practices” overlaps with prior NACo roles; emphasize what is new or more senior here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/outcome summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to lead with highest-impact achievements: website migration, analytics stack expansion, in-house studio build, governance/operations.
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add email open/click growth, social engagement/follower growth, video output, cost savings, or production volume if available.
- Tighten phrasing for concision, e.g. “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; differentiate this role as enterprise leadership, budget, systems, and modernization.
- Video leadership also appears in earlier NACo roles; emphasize building the studio and scaling in-house production capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like support than leadership. Tighten it to emphasize scope, channel ownership, and systems/process impact distinct from the later director role.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to show ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Make bullets parallel and outcome-oriented:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Coordinated editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams to improve alignment and publishing cadence.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency, speed and cross-team coordination.
- If possible, add metrics: open rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or number of teams/stakeholders supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; differentiate this entry as scaling/formalizing the program.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strategically in the 2022–2024 director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning

Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/freelance experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad terms with sharper, leadership-level language: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise digital communications strategy”; “Audience-focused content planning” → “Audience and journey-based content strategy.”
- Make the list more distinctive and concise:
- Enterprise digital communications strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience and journey-based content strategy
- If space allows, align wording to recent impact areas: consider “Web modernization and editorial governance” instead of separate generic items.
- Keep this section skills-only; save outcomes like 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, and 50+ publishers for Work Experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Editorial systems and governance” duplicates “Digital governance & editorial systems” in Core Competencies.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple recent role bullets; avoid repeating exact phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to modernization and delivery rather than listing every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming

- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production

Quick assessment: This skills item is relevant, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps with the broader “Multimedia & live event production” competency. It would be stronger if framed around delivery scope and recent leadership-level capability shown in the NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic nouns with sharper, outcome-oriented skill phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “PTZ camera and studio system operation.”

- Broadcast-quality video production & editing
- Livestream, hybrid & virtual event delivery
- PTZ camera systems & multi-camera workflows
- Studio buildout, operations & run-of-show production
- If space allows, align wording with proven experience from NACo’s in-house studio and recurring advocacy programming.

- Overlaps with Core Competencies: “Multimedia & live event production.”
- “Studio operations” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” are already implied by recent work experience; avoid repeating them elsewhere verbatim.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and partially duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/current platforms or add light proficiency context.

Suggested edit
- Prioritize most relevant/current tools first: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider “Drupal (enterprise, migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add level/scope rather than just names: e.g., “Drupal (enterprise CMS, migrations, modular content) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Keep phrasing platform-focused only; avoid adding modernization, APIs, or workflow language here since those are covered elsewhere.
- If Drupal is your clear flagship platform from recent roles, make that explicit by leading with it and adding a qualifier.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor compared with enterprise CMS experience; cut it if you need space or want a more senior emphasis.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support your recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as execution-focused tools, e.g.: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group operational tools separately: “Technical integrations & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- If accurate, add scope/outcome context in brief parentheticals, e.g. “Google Tag Manager (tracking deployment), GitHub Actions (build/deployment automation)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the rest of the CV uses that style; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing
- If Cloudflare Workers or GitHub Actions were materially used in recent roles, mention them in a recent experience bullet instead of relying only on the skills list

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. Given the stronger, more recent experience in systems architecture and digital operations, this item should emphasize automation/building platforms over basic collaboration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems
- Reorder by relevance/strength: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams
- Remove lower-value or older-feeling tools unless central to target roles: Basecamp, Trello
- If accurate, add light qualifiers to show depth, e.g. “Airtable (workflow/database systems) • Power Automate (Microsoft 365 automation) • Zapier (cross-platform integrations)”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language here.
- Slack/Teams/Asana overlap with general coordination skills, so keep only if they support a systems/operations positioning.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platform list, but it’s too bare to show level of ownership or strategic relevance. Since recent roles emphasize email operations and enterprise communications, this item should signal campaign/CRM capability rather than read like a generic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing, CRM & Member Engagement Systems
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers: enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, member communications
- Best upgrade: move one concrete outcome into recent experience instead of here, e.g., newsletter scale, automation improvements, or engagement/reporting gains

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with Work Experience entries already covering email leadership; avoid repeating “managed newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here
- If Dynamics 365 was central in recent consulting work, consider mentioning it there for stronger impact than in skills alone

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and repeats platforms already evidenced in the recent Director role. Tighten it to emphasize methods and business use, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Analytics, Reporting & Optimization
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI reporting • SEO analysis • Experimentation
- Replace “A/B testing” with “Experimentation” unless you’ve run formal tests; it reads broader and safer.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI reporting” or “Executive dashboards” to sound more outcome-oriented and senior.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item is nearly identical to “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider trimming one or making this version more technical.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already called out in the 2022–2024 Director role, so avoid repeating the exact same framing elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts,” production scope, and team-building contributions.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to stress foundational impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows for web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership and outputs: “Supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and a recurring weekly video update; coordinated day-to-day digital production across channels.”
- Tighten the management line: “Provided day-to-day supervision and training for a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience reach, publishing volume, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; here, frame it as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later roles; in this older entry, position it as helping establish baseline processes.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia work, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it shorter, emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator, and tie the research/project work to organizational impact if possible.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; helped translate findings into digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and tighten phrasing: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- If possible, add a measurable outcome: number of episodes, audience growth, internal adoption, or how it expanded NACo’s communications capabilities.
- Remove generic wording like “contributed to digital content production” unless you can specify formats or purpose.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on research support + first podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating broad web/email/social responsibilities already covered in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities and overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work bullets. Tighten it into tool-specific skills and keep broader production capabilities elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Creative & Audio/Video Tools”
- Replace with a cleaner, tool-led list: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator”
- If you want one capability included, make it specific: “Livestream production software/workflows” instead of “Livestream studio workflows”
- Remove “Podcast production” here unless paired with a platform/tool; it’s a function already evidenced in work experience
